title: Randomization and low-degree projection
statement: Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, let $f$ be a real-valued function on its outcome space, and fix an outcome $x$. As functions of $r\in\{0,1\}^n$, randomizing the low-degree projection of $f$ through level $k$ at $x$ equals the Fourier–Walsh projection through level $k$ of the function $r\mapsto R_rf(x)$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses
$f$ is real-valued on the product outcome space
$x$ is an outcome in the product space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $k\in\mathbb N$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and $x\in\Omega$. Then $r\mapsto R_r(f^{\le k})(x)$ is the Fourier projection to levels at most $k$ of the function $r\mapsto R_rf(x)$ on the uniform Boolean sign cube.
